Messages.Body:
On VTES-L, salem christ wrote:
> you once said that heidlburg couldn't be tapped to swap stuff around during
> a hostile takeover bid. now, we thought this was because the bidding was
> all part of the card's resolution, and as such there was no place after the
> card was played and before the bidding to introduce any other effects.
> ok, and then recently you said that sudden reversal is played after the
> vampire is named for hostile, but before the bidding. is this right?

By way of example:
Burning a vampire in torpor is part of Vulnerability's resolution.
Even so, Sudden Reversal is played between the time that Vuln. is
played (with the requesite nomination of victim) and the time that
it resolves. Likewise for Hostile Takeover.

> if so, does this mean that one could also tap heidlburg after the vampire
> has been named but before the bidding?

Good question. I was about to say "yes", but remembered that you
can't interupt the play-resolve sequence (except with Sudden Reversal).

HC cannot be tapped between the play-resolve sequence of HT, any more than
it could be tapped between the time a second HC was played and put into play.
